setup.pitch: Low on food and one day from the nearest village, the party reaches Briar Hollow just as a badly scratched hunter returns carrying a massive owlbear egg. Three villagers argue over whether to eat it, raise it, or return it. Before they can decide, the enraged father owlbear tears into the village.
setup.gmSummary: The adventure has one spine: force the hungry party into Briar Hollow, reveal the stolen owlbear egg, let three NPCs argue three solutions, interrupt the debate with the father owlbear attack, expose the fake druid, then branch only when the party decides the egg's fate. If the party feeds the father their last rations, he leaves and they go hungry. If they kill him, the mother answers from the ridge and later enters a barbarian-like rage. If they refuse to intervene, the father destroys Briar Hollow. Eat the egg and the mother attacks at dawn. Keep the egg and it hatches and imprints on a random present PC/NPC. Return it or leave it at the village edge and the mother retrieves it; it hatches, then mother and hatchling attack the village.
setup.background: The party has only its final day of trail food left when the road points toward Briar Hollow, itself nearly out of food. Torren Vale, the village hunter, failed to find game and instead stole a huge owlbear egg from a nest. One parent raked his face as he escaped. Mara Dell wants to cook it. Torren, shaken by what he did, wants to raise the hatchling and make the theft mean something. Elmorrow Reed presents himself as a druid and argues that he should return the egg to nature, but he is actually an animal broker for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie. The father follows Torren's scent and the egg into town.

quest.objective: Survive the owlbear family's response to the stolen egg and decide what Briar Hollow will do with it.
quest.stakes: The party's remaining food, the survival of Briar Hollow, a living owlbear family, and the party's responsibility for whichever solution they choose.
quest.deadline: The father attacks during the village debate. The egg hatches by the following morning.
successConditions: The party responds to the father owlbear attack.
The party learns enough to understand Elmorrow's real motive or knowingly accepts the risk of trusting him.
The party makes a deliberate choice about the egg and resolves the resulting consequence.
failureConditions: The party knowingly refuses to intervene while the father destroys Briar Hollow.
The party abandons the egg decision after the village has paid the price for the theft.

facts.text: Briar Hollow is nearly out of food, just like the party.
Torren stole the owlbear egg from a nest; the long scratch across his face came from one of its parents.
Mara wants to eat the egg, Torren wants to raise it, and Elmorrow claims he wants to return it.
Elmorrow is not a druid. He intends to sell the live egg or hatchling to the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.
The father owlbear will stop the attack and leave if given the party's remaining rations.
Killing the father provokes an answering scream from his mate on the ridge.
The mother enters a barbarian-like maternal rage when she attacks after the loss or theft of her family.
If the party keeps the egg, the hatchling imprints on a random present player character or named NPC.

secrets.text: Elmorrow's wagon contains a signed acquisition contract for one live juvenile owlbear, a collapsible beast crate, and sedatives.
secrets.revealCondition: Solve or force the wagon strongbox, inspect the crate hardware, or catch Elmorrow trying to leave with the egg.

locations.name: Road to Briar Hollow
locations.description: A hungry day's march from the nearest settlement, with scrub woods and a narrow bridge behind the party.

locations.name: Briar Hollow Square
locations.description: A poor village square beside a granary, bakehouse, stable, and small well.

locations.name: Mara's Bakehouse
locations.description: The safest warm room in the village and the obvious place to cook or incubate the egg.

locations.name: Elmorrow's Green Wagon
locations.description: A healer-looking wagon with a collapsible beast crate hidden beneath the tarp and a puzzle-locked strongbox.

locations.name: Edge of Briar Hollow
locations.description: A low stone wall and open field between the village and the wooded ridge.

scenes.title: One Day From Food
scenes.purpose: Get the hungry party to Briar Hollow without creating an adventure branch before the adventure starts.
scenes.readAloud:
By midday, the last of your trail food feels painfully light in your packs. A weather-beaten sign points east: BRIAR HOLLOW — ONE DAY.

The road west is longer. The forest path north is unmarked. Whatever you choose, you will be choosing it hungry.
gmNotes: The party has exactly one day of travel rations left between them for the purpose of this adventure.
If they choose Briar Hollow, move on immediately.
If they choose any other route, use the orc warband to close that path. This is a boundary threat, not the adventure's first tactical fight.
Telegraph overwhelming numbers before damage. If they retreat, they reach Briar Hollow. If they knowingly insist on a suicidal stand after the warning, a TPK is possible.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Establish that food is nearly gone and Briar Hollow is the nearest settlement.

runSteps.title: Ask where they go
runSteps.text: If they choose Briar Hollow, advance. If not, bring the orc warband onto the alternate road.

runSteps.title: Push, do not detour
runSteps.text: Make the warband obviously overwhelming and drive retreat toward Briar Hollow. Do not spend the session on this threat.

exitChoices.label: Enter Briar Hollow
exitChoices.description: The village is nearly as hungry as the party.

scenes.title: The Hunter Comes Home
scenes.purpose: Reveal the stolen egg and put the three competing solutions in front of the players before the father interrupts.
scenes.readAloud:
Briar Hollow does not look like a place with food to spare. The communal pot is thin enough to see the bottom, and the granary doors stand open on nearly empty bins.

A shout rises at the south lane. Torren Vale, the village hunter, staggers into the square carrying an egg almost as large as his chest. A fresh claw mark runs from his temple to his jaw.

“I found food,” he says, breathing hard.

The egg knocks once from the inside.
gmNotes: Torren first says he found the egg. Anyone who asks about the scratch or succeeds on Insight DC 10 gets the truth: he stole it from an owlbear nest.
Three positions: Mara says eat it. Torren says raise it. Elmorrow says let him return it to nature.
Elmorrow should initially sound like the cleanest moral answer.
Sella moderates. She is not a fourth option.
Do not resolve the debate. The father attack interrupts it.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Show the village's hunger, Torren's scratch, and the giant living egg.

runSteps.title: Reveal the theft
runSteps.text: Questioning Torren or Insight DC 10 gets the admission: he stole the egg from an active owlbear nest.

runSteps.title: Present exactly three options
runSteps.text: Mara: eat it. Torren: raise it. Elmorrow: he will return it.

runSteps.title: Let players argue briefly
runSteps.text: Give each NPC one strong argument. Keep Elmorrow credible.

runSteps.title: Interrupt with violence
runSteps.text: Before a final decision, the father owlbear crashes into the village.

scenes.advanceWhen: The three options are understood and the father attack interrupts the debate.

exitChoices.label: The father crashes into the village
exitChoices.description: Run the feed, fight, or do-nothing consequence.

scenes.title: The Father Tears Through Briar Hollow
scenes.purpose: Make the party spend its last food, fight, or accept the destruction of the village.
scenes.readAloud:
The argument ends with a roof beam exploding inward.

A massive owlbear crashes through the side of the stable, feathers slick with mud and blood. Two villagers snatch up boar spears and rush it. The first spear snaps. The owlbear swats one villager across the square and closes its beak around the second before anyone can shout a warning.

Then it smells your food.
gmNotes: If the party does nothing, the father kills the spear villagers, smashes the granary and bakehouse, and destroys Briar Hollow. Take the village-destroyed branch.
If the party throws its remaining rations, the father immediately stops attacking, devours them, and leaves. The party goes without food; the village cannot replace the rations.
If the party kills the father, the meat is not the point. Immediately answer with the mother's scream from the ridge.
Creative solutions are allowed, but resolve them back into one of three states: father leaves alive, father dies, or village is destroyed.
Do not apply starvation exhaustion immediately just because the party skipped one meal; use normal food-deprivation rules if time extends beyond this adventure.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Make the villagers' failed spear charge demonstrate that ignoring the father has consequences.

runSteps.title: Ask what the players do
runSteps.text: The core choices are give up the last rations, fight, or stand aside.

runSteps.title: If they feed him
runSteps.text: No check. He eats all remaining party rations and leaves the village. The party will be hungry.

runSteps.title: If they fight
runSteps.text: Run the father stat block below. If he dies, immediately play the mother's scream.

runSteps.title: If they do nothing
runSteps.text: Do not soft-pedal it. He destroys the village; advance to the failure resolution.

scenes.advanceWhen: The father leaves, dies, or destroys Briar Hollow.

exitChoices.label: The party intervened
exitChoices.description: The village survives. Continue with the egg and Elmorrow.

exitChoices.label: The party does nothing
exitChoices.description: The father destroys Briar Hollow. Resolve the failure ending.

scenes.title: The Druid Is Too Ready to Leave
scenes.purpose: Expose Elmorrow before the egg decision without creating a separate investigative branch.
scenes.readAloud:
As the village counts its wounded, Elmorrow is already hitching his green wagon.

“We have seen what comes of keeping this creature here,” he says. “Give me the egg. I can return it before the mother comes.”

Under the wagon tarp, something heavy shifts with the metallic rattle of a cage.
gmNotes: Point the party at the wagon. Do not require them to invent the investigation.
The strongbox puzzle is player-facing. Correct order: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN.
Inside is the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie contract for one live juvenile owlbear, sedatives, and a handler token.
If the party skips the puzzle, the crate stamp or Elmorrow's attempt to flee reveals enough truth. The fake druid twist must not be missable.
If trusted despite evidence, Elmorrow can take the egg; treat that as the keep/lose-responsibility variant, not a fourth main moral option.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Make Elmorrow's urgency and hidden cage obvious enough to investigate.

runSteps.title: Run the strongbox puzzle
runSteps.text: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN. Let the players solve it before offering rolls.

runSteps.title: Use fail-forward if needed
runSteps.text: Thieves' tools DC 13 or Strength DC 14 opens it. Failure still exposes the crate stamp/contract.

runSteps.title: Reveal the lie
runSteps.text: Elmorrow is not returning the owlbear; he intends to sell it to the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.

runSteps.title: Return to the real choice
runSteps.text: Now the party decides the egg's fate without a false clean option.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party understands Elmorrow's real motive.

exitChoices.label: Decide the egg's fate
exitChoices.description: Eat it, keep it, or return/leave it for the mother.

scenes.title: Three Choices, No Clean Answer
scenes.purpose: Branch the adventure only now, when the players actually choose what happens to the egg.
scenes.readAloud:
The egg sits in the middle of Mara's worktable, warm enough to fog the cold air. A new crack has appeared near the broad end.

Mara folds her arms. Torren touches the bandage across his face. Sella says nothing.

Outside, somewhere beyond the dark ridge, an owlbear answers the night.
gmNotes: There are three core choices now. Do not add another branch unless the players genuinely invent one.
EAT: Mara cooks the egg. The village and party get a full meal. At dawn, the mother attacks.
KEEP: the egg hatches overnight and imprints on a random present PC or named NPC.
RETURN / LEAVE AT EDGE: the mother retrieves the egg, it hatches, and mother plus hatchling attack Briar Hollow.
Elmorrow may still bargain or flee, but he no longer controls the structure.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Bring the table back to the egg and make it clear hatching is close.

runSteps.title: Restate the three actual options
runSteps.text: Eat it. Keep/raise it. Return it or leave it for the mother.

runSteps.title: Let the players choose
runSteps.text: Do not steer them toward a preferred answer.

runSteps.title: Take the matching branch
runSteps.text: Each option has its own consequence scene. Do not resolve the ending here.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party commits to one egg choice.

exitChoices.label: Eat the egg
exitChoices.description: The village eats tonight. The mother comes at dawn.

exitChoices.label: Keep and raise the egg
exitChoices.description: The egg hatches and chooses someone.

exitChoices.label: Return it / leave it at the edge
exitChoices.description: The mother retrieves it, it hatches, and the village faces the consequence.

scenes.title: Dawn Comes Angry
scenes.purpose: Resolve the eat-the-egg branch with the promised mother owlbear fight.
scenes.readAloud:
For the first time in days, Briar Hollow smells like real food. The egg feeds every table in the village, and even your own empty stomachs stop aching.

At dawn, every dog in Briar Hollow begins barking at once.

The mother owlbear steps out of the mist at the edge of the square. Then she sees the shell fragments.
gmNotes: Run the mother in Maternal Rage from the start.
If the father was killed, describe her rage as even more personal, but do not stack a second mechanical rage.
Maternal Rage: advantage on Strength checks/saves, +2 Strength-melee damage, resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing for 1 minute.
This is the cost of the eat branch: they got the food, and now they must survive the mother.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Pay off the meal, then reveal the mother at dawn.

runSteps.title: Start the mother already raging
runSteps.text: Use the quick combat block. Make her visibly fixate on shell fragments and the people around them.

runSteps.title: Resolve the boss fight
runSteps.text: Survive, drive her away, or evacuate the village.

runSteps.title: Close on the cost
runSteps.text: They chose food and saved people from hunger for a night, but the choice brought this fight.

scenes.advanceWhen: The mother is driven off, defeated, or the survivors escape.

scenes.title: The Baby Chooses
scenes.purpose: Resolve the keep-the-egg branch with the random imprint.
scenes.readAloud:
Sometime after midnight, the egg splits with a wet crack.

A beak pushes through first, then two oversized paws. The hatchling tumbles onto the blankets, shakes shell from its feathers, and stares at everyone in the room.

Then it chooses.
gmNotes: Make a random list of all present player characters and named NPCs. Roll once. The hatchling imprints on that person.
If the players deliberately arranged for one specific caretaker to be alone with the egg, that person is the only valid result.
The imprint is behavioral, not magical: it follows, cries when separated, and treats the chosen creature as parent/protector.
Elmorrow may try to exploit the moment if still free, but do not let him erase the chosen ending off-screen.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Let the table enjoy the hatch before determining who it chooses.

runSteps.title: Build the random list
runSteps.text: Include every present PC and named NPC unless the party deliberately isolated a caretaker.

runSteps.title: Roll the imprint
runSteps.text: The result is the hatchling's chosen parent/protector.

runSteps.title: Show the immediate consequence
runSteps.text: It follows that creature, cries when moved away, and starts looking for food.

scenes.advanceWhen: The imprint target is determined and the table understands the new responsibility.

scenes.title: The Mother Takes It Back
scenes.purpose: Resolve the return/edge branch with the mother retrieving the egg and then assaulting Briar Hollow with the hatchling.
scenes.readAloud:
You leave the egg where the field meets the ridge woods and back away toward the village wall.

The mother appears without a sound. She circles the egg once, touches her beak to the shell, and pulls it close beneath one massive forelimb.

The shell cracks.

A smaller head pushes free. The mother lifts her face toward Briar Hollow and screams.
gmNotes: The mother retrieves the egg; returning it does not produce a clean escape from consequences.
The hatchling follows its mother toward the village. It is not the main damage dealer, but it participates in the assault.
Run the mother in Maternal Rage. The party can defend Briar Hollow or evacuate rather than stand and fight.
This branch demonstrates that 'give it back' was not a guaranteed peaceful solution.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: Let the players see the apparent success before the egg hatches.

runSteps.title: Trigger the reversal
runSteps.text: The mother turns toward the village instead of leaving.

runSteps.title: Run the assault
runSteps.text: Mother is the boss; hatchling follows and harasses. Evacuation is a valid resolution.

runSteps.title: Close on consequence
runSteps.text: The family has the egg back, but the village still pays for the original theft.

scenes.advanceWhen: The village is defended, evacuated, or overrun.

scenes.title: Briar Hollow Falls
scenes.purpose: Honor the do-nothing choice with a clear failure resolution instead of pretending the adventure continues normally.
scenes.readAloud:
Nobody stops it.

The owlbear tears through the square, then the granary, then the bakehouse. The villagers who can run scatter into the fields. By the time the creature finally disappears into the smoke, Briar Hollow is no longer a village — only burning roofs, broken grain bins, and bodies in the mud.
gmNotes: This is a real failure ending. Do not quietly reset the village so the egg debate can continue.
Survivors blame Torren for the theft and the party for standing aside.
If desired, the egg may be gone with the father or buried in the ruins, but the one-shot is over.

runSteps.title: Read the boxed text
runSteps.text: State the consequence plainly.

runSteps.title: Resolve survivors
runSteps.text: Let the players help the wounded or leave, but do not reopen the main adventure.

runSteps.title: End the one-shot
runSteps.text: The choice not to act was itself the ending.

scenes.advanceWhen: The table accepts the destruction of Briar Hollow as the consequence.

encounters.name: Orc Warband on the Road
encounters.summary: If the party refuses Briar Hollow, an orc raiding column closes the alternate road and drives them toward the village.
encounters.resolution: Reach Briar Hollow. This encounter exists to close the map, not to consume the session.
encounters.special: Clearly telegraph overwhelming numbers. If players insist on a suicidal stand after warning, the warband can kill them.

encounters.name: Enraged Owlbear Father
encounters.summary: The father tracks the stolen egg into town and tears through anyone between him and it.
encounters.resolution: Feed him the party's remaining rations, kill him, drive him off creatively, or refuse to intervene.
encounters.talkOut: He cannot be reasoned with, but food overrides his rage.
encounters.bypass: Throw the party's remaining rations into the square. He devours them and leaves.
encounters.special: If the party does nothing, two spear-bearing villagers are killed immediately and the father destroys Briar Hollow. If killed, the mother's scream answers from the ridge.

encounters.name: Mother Owlbear in Maternal Rage
encounters.summary: At dawn the mother arrives enraged over the destroyed or missing egg.
encounters.resolution: Survive, drive her off, or escape the village.
encounters.talkOut: No normal social check ends the rage once combat begins.
encounters.bypass: Only available before combat by abandoning the village and egg.
encounters.special: Maternal Rage mirrors a 2014 barbarian's Rage: advantage on Strength checks and saves, +2 damage on Strength-based melee attacks, resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing damage for 1 minute.

encounters.name: Mother and Hatchling Assault
encounters.summary: The returned egg hatches in the mother's presence; instead of leaving, the mother charges Briar Hollow and the hatchling follows her aggression.
encounters.resolution: Drive the mother away, survive until she withdraws, or evacuate the village.
encounters.talkOut: Once the assault begins, the mother is in Maternal Rage.
encounters.bypass: Evacuate rather than defend the village.
encounters.special: The hatchling is weak but follows and harasses; the mother is the real threat.

puzzles.name: Shell Before Shackle
puzzles.prompt: Elmorrow's brass strongbox has four sliding picture tiles: an EGG, a CHAIN, a CIRCUS TENT, and a SILVER COIN. Scratched below them: “Shell before shackle, shackle before show; show before silver — that's how fortunes grow.” Put the tiles in order.
puzzles.failForward: Thieves' tools DC 13 or Strength DC 14 opens the box. Failure brings Elmorrow running, but his crate stamp and exposed contract still reveal the truth.

items.name: Stolen Owlbear Egg

items.name: Party's Last Rations

events.name: The Mate Answers

events.name: The Baby Chooses
events.effect: On the keep branch, roll randomly among all present PCs and named NPCs unless the party deliberately isolated one caretaker.

endings.name: Eat the Egg

endings.name: Keep and Raise It

recovery.principle: Keep the adventure on one spine. Move information forward instead of opening side branches.
policies: If the party misses a clue, deliver it in the next unavoidable scene.
Do not create a second investigation path before the father attack.
Only branch when the party's action creates a different consequence.

routes.trigger: The party refuses to go to Briar Hollow
routes.response: The orc warband closes the alternate route and drives them toward Briar Hollow.

routes.trigger: The party never confronts Torren about the scratch
routes.response: The father's arrival proves an adult owlbear tracked him and the egg; Torren blurts out the theft during the attack.

routes.trigger: The party refuses to inspect Elmorrow's wagon
routes.response: His beast crate stamp and acquisition papers fall into view as he tries to load the egg. The fake-druid truth is still exposed before the final choice.

routes.trigger: The party resolves the father with an unexpected plan
routes.response: Classify the result as father alive/leaves, father dead, or village destroyed, then continue from that state.

routes.trigger: The party invents a fourth egg solution
routes.response: Allow it only if it clearly pays a cost equivalent to one of the three core branches; otherwise ask what happens to the egg by dawn.

pathPressure.principle: The adventure stays on one spine until a real consequence branch. The ending is never locked by a missed check; the players still finish the one-shot, but their choices can produce different terminal outcomes.

prepared.when: They expose Elmorrow before choosing the egg
prepared.payoff: They make the final decision without being manipulated by the fake druid.

prepared.when: They preserve their rations by killing the father
prepared.payoff: They keep their food but provoke the mother's rage.

rushed.cost: They save the village without bloodshed but spend their last food and go hungry.

rushed.when: They do nothing during the father attack
rushed.cost: Briar Hollow is destroyed and the one-shot ends in failure.

notDeviation: Eating the egg is not failure.
Keeping the egg is not automatically kind.
Returning the egg is not automatically safe.
The fake druid is a lie, not a fourth moral answer.

oneshotRecipe.shape: linear consequence chain with one final three-way branch
oneshotRecipe.tale: A hungry party reaches a hungry village just as a stolen owlbear egg brings its family to the door.

rooms.note: Branch only here; each choice pays off.

notes: Use the SRD-style owlbear quick-run block supplied in this package. Feeding the pooled rations is an authored encounter resolution, not a spell or class feature.
Use the same encounter numbers for this adventure unless the table prefers a current SRD owlbear stat block. The authored feed-or-fight resolution is unchanged.

encounters.objective: Close the alternate road and push the party toward Briar Hollow.
encounters.start: An orc raiding column appears in overwhelming numbers on the route away from the village.

creatures.name: Orc Raiders
creatures.trait: Overwhelming Column: reinforcements continue arriving; this is not balanced as a stand-up fight.
creatures.tactics: Advance in numbers, cut off the road, and force retreat. Do not chase beyond the road to Briar Hollow.

encounters.end: The party reaches Briar Hollow or knowingly chooses a suicidal stand.

encounters.objective: Stop the father before he destroys Briar Hollow.
encounters.start: He kills or mauls the first spear-bearing villagers and turns toward the party's food scent.
encounters.bypass: Throw the party's remaining rations into the square; he eats them and leaves.

creatures.name: Owlbear Father
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +7 to hit, 1d10+5 piercing; Claws +7 to hit, 2d8+5 slashing.
creatures.trait: Food Overrides Rage: if the party offers all remaining rations, he stops attacking immediately.
creatures.tactics: Attack anyone blocking the egg or food. Smash structures if ignored.

encounters.end: Father leaves alive, dies, or the village is destroyed.

encounters.objective: Survive the mother's dawn attack after the egg is eaten.
encounters.start: She enters the square already in Maternal Rage.
encounters.bypass: Evacuate rather than defend the village.

creatures.name: Mother Owlbear
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +8 to hit, 1d10+7 piercing while raging; two Claws +8 to hit, 2d8+7 slashing each while raging.
creatures.trait: Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): advantage on Strength checks and saves; +2 damage on Strength-based melee attacks; resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
creatures.tactics: Prioritize creatures near shell remains, then anyone who damages her.

encounters.end: She is defeated, driven off, or the village is evacuated.

encounters.objective: Survive or evacuate when the returned egg hatches and the family attacks.
encounters.start: The mother retrieves the egg, the hatchling emerges, and she turns back toward Briar Hollow.

creatures.name: Mother Owlbear
creatures.attack: Multiattack: Beak +8 to hit, 1d10+7 piercing while raging; two Claws +8 to hit, 2d8+7 slashing each while raging.
creatures.trait: Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): advantage on Strength checks and saves; +2 Strength-melee damage; resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing.
creatures.tactics: Drive straight toward the village defenders while keeping the hatchling behind her.

creatures.name: Owlbear Hatchling
creatures.trait: Follow Mother: stays within 20 ft. of the mother when possible.
creatures.tactics: Snaps at nearby legs and follows the mother's target; it is not a serious damage source.

encounters.end: The mother is driven off, the village evacuates, or Briar Hollow is overrun.

rewards.when: The party feeds its final rations to the father.
rewards.reward: The village survives the attack without killing him, but cannot replace the party's food. They go hungry.
Sella gives the party a standing village favor rather than food the village does not have.
The baby owlbear imprints on a random present PC or named NPC; this is a responsibility/story reward, not a combat pet entitlement.

features: thin communal food table near center
two doomed spear villagers begin adjacent to father

mapNotes.dimensions: Village square at dawn, roughly 60 x 60 ft.
Village edge and field, roughly 80 x 60 ft.

cards.title: Baby Owlbear
cards.front: A damp, oversized owlbear hatchling with too-big paws, a snapping beak, and enormous yellow eyes.

back.location: Mara’s Bakehouse at hatching; afterward wherever its bonded PC goes.
dialogue: If separated from its bonded PC: a rising, panicked owl-like trill.
rules: Tiny Beak: +3 to hit, 1 piercing damage.
Imprint: bonds to the PC who most clearly held, fed, protected, or soothed it. If unclear, randomly select one PC.
The bond is behavioral, not magical. It follows that PC, cries when separated, steals food, and snaps at obvious threats.
Animal Handling DC 12 calms it for 1 hour.
dmNotes: Use the imprint as the final emotional beat if the egg survives.
Do not let Elmorrow steal the baby off-screen after the players earn this ending.
The baby is a responsibility, not a combat reward.

cards.imageAlt: Newly hatched baby owlbear with oversized paws, soft brown feathers, and bright yellow eyes.

cards.title: Starving Owlbear Father
cards.front: A gaunt adult owlbear with exposed ribs, ragged feathers, and foam around its beak.

back.location: Briar Hollow Square, smashing through the smokehouse toward the food table.
dialogue: No speech. Ragged hoots, wet beak-snaps, and desperate growls whenever food moves.
rules: Multiattack: Beak +7, 1d10+5 piercing; Claws +7, 2d8+5 slashing.
Feverish Hunger: offer the party’s pooled one-day rations and he immediately stops attacking, eats, and leaves.
Throwing the rations from 20 ft. works automatically. Placing them beside him safely: Animal Handling DC 12.
If killed, the carcass is visibly sick and the meat is unsafe.
dmNotes: He is starving, not evil. He prioritizes visible food over creatures whenever possible.
If he dies, immediately trigger the mother’s distant scream.
Never turn the sick carcass into a food reward; that undercuts the dilemma.

cards.imageAlt: Gaunt feverish adult male owlbear with ragged feathers, visible ribs, and foam at the beak.

cards.title: Mother Owlbear
cards.front: A scarred owlbear roughly twice the father’s bulk, visible only in pieces between the ridge trees.

back.location: Ridge woods outside Briar Hollow; may approach only if the egg/hatchling is endangered or returned.
dialogue: No speech. A deep booming scream that sends birds out of the trees.
rules: Multiattack: Beak +8; two Claws +8.
Maternal Rage (1/day, 1 minute): advantage on Strength checks/saves; +2 Strength-melee damage; resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing.
Eat branch: she attacks at dawn.
Return branch: she retrieves the egg, it hatches, and she leads the hatchling back against the village.
dmNotes: She is the physical consequence of the egg choice, not an optional random encounter.
Keep her rage simple and equivalent to a 2014 barbarian's core Rage benefits.
Evacuation is a valid resolution when she attacks.

cards.imageAlt: Enormous scarred mother owlbear on a dark forest ridge, nearly twice the father’s bulk.

cards.title: Mayor Sella Vane
cards.front: A sleepless mayor gripping a ration ledger hard enough to bend its cover.

back.location: Village Square, Granary, and final egg debate.
dialogue: “If there were a good answer, we’d have found it before you got here.”
“I don’t need pretty. I need survivable.”
“Tomorrow, we live with what we decided tonight.”
rules: Knows the true ration count: about 2½ days remain.
Investigation DC 12 on the ledger reveals her own household has taken less than its share.
She accepts any deliberate ending, even one she dislikes.
dmNotes: Play her as fair, exhausted, and unsentimental—not cold.
She prevents the crowd from becoming a mob while the party investigates.
Never use her to declare which moral choice is correct.

cards.imageAlt: Exhausted village mayor holding a worn ration ledger in both hands.

cards.title: Mara Dell
cards.front: A flour-dusted baker with a cleaver on the table and hungry children on her mind.

back.role: Strongest argument for cooking the egg
dialogue: “You can’t feed a village with ideals.”
“One proper meal. Tomorrow we are hungry again.”
“Warm shell or not, I’ve got children chewing bark.”
rules: Knows exactly how far the remaining food can stretch.
Confirms the father’s carcass is unusable if he dies.
Will cook the egg if the final decision goes that way, but will not seize it herself.
dmNotes: Do not portray Mara as cruel. Her position should remain morally defensible.
She openly admits the omelet buys only one communal meal plus broth.
Her strongest scenes are short, practical statements rather than speeches.

cards.imageAlt: Flour-dusted village baker beside a worktable, with a cleaver resting flat rather than raised.

cards.title: Torren Vale
cards.front: A soot-stained woodsman with cut rope, stained blankets, and exactly the wrong-looking knife.

back.role: Hunter who stole the egg / advocates raising it
back.location: Village Square and final egg debate.
dialogue: “I thought it was food until it moved.”
“I stole it. I know what that makes me.”
“If we crack it now, then all I brought home was another corpse.”
rules: Long fresh scratch across his face came from an adult owlbear during the theft.
Insight DC 10: his 'found it' story is false; he stole the egg from an active nest.
His position is to keep and raise the hatchling.
dmNotes: He is not the red herring anymore; his guilt is real and obvious.
Use him to reveal the theft quickly, not to create another investigation branch.
He should sound shaken rather than heroic.

cards.imageAlt: Soot-stained charcoal burner carrying cut rope, stained blankets, and a hooked woods knife.

cards.title: Elmorrow Reed
cards.front: A moss-cloaked 'druid' with polished nature sayings and a green wagon parked too close to the egg.

back.role: Red-herring 'return it' advocate / hidden circus broker
back.location: Village Square, then his green wagon after the father attack.
dialogue: “The kindest thing is to return it to the wild.”
“Give it to me. I know where creatures like this belong.”
When exposed: “A cage is safer than a grave.”
rules: Nature DC 12: his druid lore is shallow and rehearsed.
Strongbox puzzle: EGG → CHAIN → TENT → COIN.
Wagon evidence proves he works for the Moonpetal Traveling Menagerie.
If exposed, he bargains or flees rather than becoming a boss fight.
dmNotes: He is the misleading 'clean' answer during the first debate.
The fake-druid reveal happens after the father attack, before the true egg choice.
Do not let his lie become a permanent fourth branch.

cards.imageAlt: Moss-cloaked false druid with a polished wooden staff beside a green animal-handler wagon.

flowContract.principle: One linear spine. Branch only when a player choice creates a genuinely different consequence.
